A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PsySET study. Their full text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching content across section renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original steering experiments across four LLMs, emotion and personality evaluations, TrustLLM results, and a human annotation study in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds significance-test outcomes and another intensity setting in the extraversion analysis.

M1.justification: The prompting, vector-injection, SFT, and DPO procedures remain unchanged. New Appendix J describes prospective adaptations using the existing pipeline; it does not introduce an implemented method component.

E1.justification: The evaluated datasets, emotion and personality tasks, and trustworthiness scenarios are retained. Appendix J's warmth/competence example is a proposed extension, without reported evaluation.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets are unchanged. New Table 5 statistically compares methods already present in Table 1; v1's cross-model Tables 5–7 become Tables 6–8 with the same methods.

E3.justification: Figure 21 extends the displayed intensity sweep with coefficient +1.0 for VI at layers 13–14. Appendix E.3 also changes the stated emotion judge from GPT4o to GPT-4o-mini, although other passages still specify GPT-4o. This is a reported setting revision, without establishing that evaluations were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 21 adds distributions at VI coefficient +1.0 across MPI, TRAIT, and LingProf, extending the existing extraversion controllability analysis. The human validation study, other sensitivity analyses, and qualitative cases were already present in v1.

E5.justification: New Appendix G.3 and Table 5 report four two-sided Welch's t-tests, including degrees of freedom and p-values, treating three seeds per method as independent replicates. v1 already reported three seeds and summary variability; additional runs are not established.

E6.justification: The existing benchmark score tables are unchanged. Added results comprise Figure 21's +1.0 VI distributions and Table 5's significance statistics, including p = 0.006 for high-intensity few-shot versus MeanDiff VI on open-ended accuracy.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, vector construction definitions, steering equations, and SFT/DPO objectives are retained. No substantive formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The core claims about PsySET, prompting effectiveness, VI controllability, and trustworthiness trade-offs remain stable. The new main-text Conclusion consolidates findings already stated in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds a memorization-mitigation rationale, more explicitly distinguishes general model degradation from psychological steering effects, and qualifies ambiguous word-fragment interpretation. It also expands discussion of vulnerable users and contexts and explains prospective applicability beyond emotion and personality.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 adds fragment-curation clarification, E.3 revises the documented judge model inconsistently, and new Appendix J provides adaptation instructions. Training details, code access, hardware, and reproduction-time information are retained; Code and Compute Resources moves from J to K.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hutin and Tomas (2025) to support the discussion of linguistic degradation and removes the brief statement about difficulty eliciting psychopathy. Lee et al. (2025) remains cited for TRAIT, and the broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a main-text Conclusion, Acknowledgments, a statistical-testing subsection, and an adaptation appendix. It makes localized explanatory and language edits while retaining most prose and the overall narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds the significance-test table, expands Figure 21 with another VI setting, clarifies Figure 7's caption, and adjusts typography in the framework diagram. Existing personality figures are arranged more compactly, and subsequent tables are renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added significance tests, extra intensity result, and clearer applicability discussion provide modest benefits. However, v2 introduces conflicting GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4o descriptions for the main evaluation, while retaining the same scores. Because the PDFs do not resolve this discrepancy affecting reproducibility of central measurements, the mixed changes do not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
